summary: Egypt’s restoration pledge is to rehabilitate and line 20,000 km of irrigation canals, with drainage-system rehabilitation also planned to support agricultural climate resilience and conserve water. Its agriculture pledge covers 4 million feddans with modern surface irrigation, aims to raise agricultural water-use efficiency by 20%, and combines tolerant crops with soil maintenance and protection from degradation. Conservation commitments seek protectorates covering 17% of national marine and wildlife areas, including at least a 5% coastal component, plus sustainable parks in new cities of 5–20 feddans. In context, the country is overwhelmingly bare area (91.3%; 917,370 km²), while agriculture covers 48,963 km² (4.9%); forest and grassland are just 7 and 9 km², respectively. Thus, the quantified pledges focus on irrigation networks, agricultural production and protected areas rather than large-scale forest or grassland restoration.
